    Interrupted time series for a corpus outcome

    Source: R/its.R
    sm_its.Rd

    A turnkey interrupted time series (ITS): aggregates the chosen outcome to a yearly series, fits a segmented regression with a level shift and a slope change at intervention_year, and derives the counterfactual (the pre-intervention trend projected forward).

    Usage

    sm_its(
  corpus,
  intervention_year,
  outcome = c("count", "share_q1", "cnci", "leadership"),
  family = NULL,
  lag = NULL,
  institutions = NULL,
  lead_role = c("corresponding", "first", "last", "first_or_last", "any_lead"),
  min_cell = NULL,
  call = rlang::caller_env()
)

# S3 method for class 'sm_its'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sm_its'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sm_its'
autoplot(object, ...)

    Arguments

    corpus

    An sm_corpus.

    intervention_year

    Year at which the intervention takes effect: one whole number such as 2020, or text holding one.

    outcome

    One of "count", "share_q1", "cnci", "leadership". The expected source columns are:

    "count"

    Works per year (uses works$year).

    "share_q1"

    Share of Q1-journal works among the works with a quartile; needs a journal-quartile column on works (quartile, jif_quartile, or sjr_quartile).

    "cnci"

    Mean field-normalised citation impact per year. Impact is resolved from the first populated of works$cnci, works$fwci (OpenAlex; see sm_enrich_openalex_impact()), the other impact columns fnci, rcr, cnci_value, ncs, mncs and field_citation_ratio, a corpus$metrics table (cnci/fnci/value keyed by work_id), or works$cited_by_count (from which FNCI is derived via sm_metric_fnci(), with min_cell). If none is populated, an informative error (class scimapR_no_impact_data) names the columns inspected. sm_metric_summary() (metric = "cnci") resolves impact in the same order, and the result names the source used (impact_source). Works without a finite impact value are left out of the yearly mean.

    "leadership"

    Share of works led through the author role lead_role (by default the corresponding author, authorships$is_corresponding), by one of institutions when they are given; see Details.

    family

    Optional GLM family (a family object, generator function, or name). Defaults to Poisson for "count" and Gaussian otherwise; document your choice when overriding. A Poisson fit warns when the counts are overdispersed; "quasipoisson" then scales the standard errors.

    lag

    Citation-maturity lag in years (default 2). For citation-based outcomes ("cnci"), the most recent lag years are citation-immature and are excluded from the fit; this is reported in the print method.

    institutions

    For outcome = "leadership": NULL (default) or a character vector of focal institution labels. A work then counts as led when an authorship in the role lead_role belongs to one of them, that is when its institution_match, institution_name or institution_id, or the name of that id in corpus$institutions, is one of the labels (run sm_affiliation_match() first). A label that no authorship carries gives a warning naming the nearest labels; when none is found, sm_its() aborts.

    lead_role

    For outcome = "leadership": the author role that leads a work. "corresponding" (default) is an author with is_corresponding = TRUE, "first" and "last" are the authors with the lowest and the highest position of the work, "first_or_last" either, and "any_lead" the first, last or corresponding author. Roles other than "corresponding" need institutions.

    min_cell

    For outcome = "cnci": NULL (default) or a positive integer, passed to sm_metric_fnci() when the impact is derived from works$cited_by_count, so that works in field-year cells with fewer works fall back to larger baselines. Not used when the corpus carries stored impact values.

    call

    Caller environment for error reporting.

    x

    An sm_its object.

    ...

    Ignored.

    object

    An sm_its object.

    Value

    An sm_its S3 object with components: model (the fitted glm), coefficients (tidy tibble: term, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high, statistic, p.value), series (tibble: year, observed, fitted, counterfactual), and metadata (outcome, intervention_year, family, lag, provisional_years, dropped_years, leadership). dropped_years (integer) lists the years left out for lack of a usable value, provisional_years (integer) the citation-immature years excluded after them. leadership holds the definition used for outcome = "leadership", a list of lead_role, institution_aware (FALSE), institutions (the focal labels or NULL) and label_column (the column that labels the institutions of the corpus, institution_match, institution_name or institution_id, the first with a value; NA without institutions), and is NULL for the other outcomes. impact_source (character) names where the impact values of outcome = "cnci" come from, such as "works$fwci (OpenAlex)" or "works$cited_by_count (field-normalised)"; NA for the other outcomes.

    print returns x invisibly.

    summary returns the tidy coefficient tibble.

    autoplot returns a ggplot.

    Details

    The yearly series is built first. For "count" it runs over every year from the first to the last publication year of the corpus, and a year without works counts 0, so filter the corpus to the analysis window beforehand. For the other outcomes a year with works but no usable value is dropped with a warning and listed in dropped_years: no work of the year has a journal quartile ("share_q1") or a finite impact value ("cnci"). For "cnci" the citation-immature years are excluded after that and listed in provisional_years, so no year is in both.

    For "leadership" the share of a year is over the works whose lead is known, and that number of works weights the year in the fit. A work whose authorships all have is_corresponding = NA (unknown, as the readers of sources without corresponding-author data record it; see sm_corpus()) leaves the denominator for lead_role = "corresponding", with or without institutions; up to scimapR 0.4.0 it counted as not led. So does a work without authorships, and for the position roles a work whose positions are all NA. For "any_lead" an unknown corresponding author counts as not leading, so the work stays in the denominator. A year in which no work has a known lead is dropped with a warning, and sm_its() aborts when no work has one. With institutions the denominator is every work of the year with a known lead, not only the works with an authorship at the focal institutions.

    A focal label is compared with every label column of an authorship row (institution_match, institution_name, institution_id and the name of that id), as group membership in sm_did() and sm_synth() is, so a row with institution_match "A" and institution_name "B" belongs to both "A" and "B". sm_count() instead labels each row by the first of these columns with a value. The print method names the column that labels the institutions of the corpus (leadership$label_column).

    At least 4 years must remain after these exclusions, with 2 or more before intervention_year and 2 or more from it on, so that the pre-trend, the level change and the slope change can all be estimated; otherwise sm_its() aborts. With only 4 years the 4 coefficients fit the series exactly: a family that estimates its dispersion (Gaussian, quasi families) then has no residual degrees of freedom, so its standard errors, intervals and p-values are NaN and sm_its() warns. Families that fix the dispersion, such as the Poisson default for "count", keep their standard errors.

    The confidence intervals are Wald intervals on the reference distribution of the p-values: t with the residual degrees of freedom when the family estimates its dispersion (Gaussian and quasi families), normal when the family fixes it (Poisson, binomial). The standard errors treat the yearly values as independent; no correction for autocorrelation is applied.

    See also

    sm_did(), sm_citation_maturity()

    Other causal: sm_did(), sm_synth()

    Examples

    corpus <- sm_example_corpus(n_works = 200, seed = 1)
its <- sm_its(corpus, intervention_year = 2020, outcome = "count")
its
#> 
#> ── <sm_its> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Outcome: count Family: poisson
#> Intervention year: 2020
#> 
#> 
#> ── Segmented regression coefficients 
#> Baseline level: 3.0063 [2.6712, 3.3413] (p = <2e-16)
#> Pre-trend (slope): 0.0236 [-0.1111, 0.1583] (p = 0.73)
#> Level change: -0.2997 [-0.8709, 0.2714] (p = 0.3)
#> Slope change: 0.0297 [-0.1669, 0.2262] (p = 0.77)
# \donttest{
ggplot2::autoplot(its)

# }

# share of works whose corresponding author is at a focal unit
fix <- readRDS(sm_example_files("example_realuse_corpus.rds"))
dict <- readr::read_csv(
  sm_example_files("example_realuse_affiliation_dict.csv"),
  col_types = "ccc"
)
fix <- sm_affiliation_match(fix, dict)
#> ✔ Affiliation matching flagged 427 authorships across 4 institutions.
#> ℹ By signal: name_token: 427. See `sm_affiliation_summary()` for the full
#>   breakdown.
lead <- sm_its(fix, intervention_year = 2021, outcome = "leadership",
               institutions = "Armed Forces Hospital Northtown")
lead$series
#> # A tibble: 11 × 4
